transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, I came in because my mind just feels really foggy lately. I work at the library, and I can't even seem to keep my place in my old cataloguing notes. It's gotten to the point where I just... I can't even decide what simple thing to do next.
{"intent":"Determine the time course of the cognitive changes","question":"When did you first notice this mental fogginess?""}
It's been going on for about three weeks now. It started right after that first rush of retirement faded away... that's when I really noticed this whole shift happening.
Do you notice that the fogginess comes and goes, or is it present at about the same level all day?

I haven't really noticed it coming and going, to be honest. It just... it seems to be there pretty much all day. I haven't really paid attention to whether it gets better or worse at certain hours, it just feels like a constant struggle from the time I wake up.
During these past three weeks, have you been feeling persistently sad, down, or empty?

Yeah, I have. Most days lately, I just sit at the kitchen table and... well, it feels like the color has just gone out of everything. Even my old watercolor books, which I usually enjoy, they just make me feel heavy instead of interested now. So yes, I've definitely been feeling pretty down and empty.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or lacking energy most days during these past three weeks?

I wouldn't really say I'm unusually tired, no. I mean, I'm sitting around a lot more, but it's not because my body feels exhausted or drained of energy. I just... I just don't have the drive to do much of anything right now. But my physical energy itself seems about normal, I just haven't been using it.
During these past three weeks, have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead or of harming yourself?

No, I haven't had any thoughts like that. I know I've been feeling pretty low and empty, like I mentioned, but... no, I haven't thought about harming myself or dying. It's just a heavy feeling, not anything like that.
Have you noticed any change in your sleep since this began?

Yeah, there's been a change. I go to bed tired enough, but... then I end up waking up around four in the morning. I just lie there in the dark, thinking about what I'm supposed to do with myself now. I can't really seem to get back to sleep after that.
During these past three weeks, have you been feeling worthless or excessively guilty about things?

No, I wouldn't say I feel worthless or guilty. I mean, I feel kind of down and empty, like I said before, but I don't feel like I've done anything wrong or that I'm a burden to anyone. I just feel... flat, I guess. But no guilt or anything like that.
Since this began, have you noticed any change in your appetite?

Yeah, it has. I don't really feel hungry lately. I actually have to remind myself to eat most days. My wife has been noticing it, too... she points out that I leave my rice and soup half-finished. Before all this, I would never waste a meal, I'd always clear my plate. But now, I just don't really have the desire for it.
How much have these changes interfered with your ability to manage your usual daily responsibilities?

Well, they've interfered a fair amount. I mean... I've let a lot of things pile up lately. Things like lecture plans, some travel notes, and even just simple household paperwork. I look at it all and I just... I can't reliably organize myself the way I used to. It's all just sitting there on my desk, and I can't seem to get it sorted out.
Do your low mood and loss of interest mainly occur when you think about retiring, or do they persist even when retirement is not on your mind?

It's pretty much all the time, honestly. It doesn't really matter if I'm thinking about retiring or not. Even when I'm just sitting at home or trying to focus on something else, that low, flat feeling is still there. It's not tied to any one specific thought like that.
